text:
natalie: Customer (Acme) opened CS-4821 — multiple 503s on hosted inference during long streamed responses. Started ~09:12 UTC. They report timeouts + intermittent 500/503.

mike: Can you paste the gateway logs around the 09:12 window?

natalie: Gateway shows repeated upstream 502 -> 503. Snippet: 
```
[09:11:58] upstream request 0x7f -> status=502 after 12000ms
[09:12:01] upstream request 0x7f -> connection reset by peer
[09:12:02] infer-runner[pid=3124] segfault (core dumped)
```

sophie: Paging @oncall — looks like an upstream infer worker crashed midstream. Could be GPU OOM or segfault during toolcall. Customer was streaming a multi-file tool call.

oncall: I'm on it. I see restart loop on that pool starting 09:12:00. Pulling container logs and nvml stats now.

jordan: From metrics: p95 latency spikes 09:10-09:13, then drops as requests fail. Memory on the node climbed steadily before crash. Could be KV-prefetch ballooning with streaming toolcall.

mike: We rolled a quantization swap to that model group at 08:45 earlier today — worth checking if compatible with toolcall codepath.

sre-bot: Incident created INC-20260318-52, alerting oncall and creating S3 dump bucket.

oncall: Crash log from runner: 
```
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_alloc'
what():  std::bad_alloc
[stack trace]
signal 11 (SIGSEGV), code 1, fault addr 0x7ff...
cuda-memcheck: device-side assert triggered
```

kevin: std::bad_alloc + device assert suggests GPU memory exhaustion during KV prefetch + ATTENTION kernel. We should capture /var/log/nvml and full dmesg.

jordan: Repro notes: customer used streaming with approx 40k token context + toolcall that does repeated embed lookups. Repro locally with smaller context and sequential toolcall loop caused same OOM on T4 sim.

mike: Mitigations applied: 1) fallback routing to lower-capacity pool (non-quantized but lower memory) 2) temporarily disable model hot-swap/quant-burst on that pool 3) throttle max concurrent streaming sessions for the customer. I've pushed the routing change.

natalie: CS update: Acme confirmed errors decreased after fallback routing. They're able to retry but still saw a single 503 during retry sequence.

oncall: Uploaded core + nvml logs to s3://redwood-incident-dumps/INC-4821/1716832345/ — core.tgz, nvml.log, dmesg.txt. Also captured gcov-style memory maps.

kevin: Next steps: devs to analyze core with gdb, check kernel ATTN kernel path for quantized kernels. Possible regression in attention kernel selection when long context + toolcall present.

mike: For immediate customer relief we should recommend reducing streaming chunk size and disable prefix prefetch on their tenant until fix. Natalie to relay.

natalie: Relayed mitigations + recommended client changes. Customer agreed to reduce longprompt chunks and will hold heavy batch repro for now.

jordan: Added repro scripts to the incident bucket and a minimal curl repro (streaming=true, toolcall loop). Snippet: 
```bash
for i in $(seq 1 20); do 
  curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate -d '{"stream":true,"input":"<long prompt>"}'
done
```

sophie: Marking as high priority — requesting assignment to eng-runtime and eng-ml for postmortem.

natalie: CS will keep the ticket open and monitor. We'll update when root cause confirmed and patch is ready.
